items.author: CryptoReviewing
items.context: @CryptoReviewing (97.103 seguidores), en inglés: un usuario de Trezor Safe 7 (sellado, semilla creada en el dispositivo y anotada en papel) dice que le drenaron ~$610.000 (~$580.000 en USDT) sin aprobar ninguna transacción. Onchain Lens: las transferencias usaron la autoridad de firma de la víctima, no un drenaje por aprobación de tokens; causa raíz no confirmada. Recuerda que hace 7 días Trezor admitió la brecha de un socio con datos de ~27.000 pedidos. Post reciente con 1.602 vistas y aún sin respuestas (creciendo). Ángulo: custodia / hardware wallets / air-gapped (libro).
items.suggested_text:
Worth separating what's confirmed from what isn't. Onchain Lens says the transfers used the victim's own signing authority, not a token-approval drain, and that no root cause has been confirmed. That narrows it to two paths: the key was exposed somewhere along the chain, or something signed with it that shouldn't have.

A sealed box and a paper seed cover two links, not all of them: how the seed was generated, every computer and app the wallet was ever paired with, and the firmware doing the signing. Add a partner breach that leaked names and home addresses from ~27,000 orders, and physical and social-engineering risk enters the picture too.

That's why I documented an air-gapped setup where keys are generated and sign on a machine that never touches the internet: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

Trusting a brand is one point of failure; the real question is how many others are sitting quietly behind it.
